weather_line: Fog holding in the hollows · amber light reported near the Ministry · biscuit tin undisturbed

stories.headline: Briefcase Acquires a Name Tag; Name Tag Is Not Quoyne's; Quoyne Is Filing This Under 'Pending'
body: Senior Archivist Percival Quoyne arrived Wednesday morning to find the glowing briefcase exactly where he had left it — on his blotter, amber-gold, thoroughly uninvited — with one addition: a small brass name tag, screwed neatly to the clasp, that had not been present the previous evening. The tag does not bear Quoyne's name. It does not bear the name of any current Ministry employee on record. The Department of Mysteries, reached for comment via a corridor-to-corridor memo, replied with a single word — 'Ah' — and withdrew.

Quoyne, who has spent eleven years filing objects that arrive without explanation and leave without permission, described the development as 'a clerical matter of moderate complexity.' The name on the tag is partially legible. Sources close to the investigation confirm only that it begins with the letter 'C' and that the engraving is 'quite good, actually — someone took their time.' The blotter remains warm. No one has tried the lock. The briefcase has begun, faintly, to hum.

stories.headline: Wednesday Client Arrives Uncertain; Departs Certain; Christine Responsible for the Difference
body: A witch presenting what she described as 'a complicated situation, possibly two complicated situations, maybe three' arrived at Christine's office Wednesday morning and was shown to a chair. By the time she left, the situations had been identified, sorted, and assigned a resolution timeline that the goblins had already — unusually — pre-approved.

Christine is understood to have said very little, consulted the ledger once, and looked at the goblins in a way that settled the matter. The client paused at the door to ask if Christine had done this before. Christine confirmed that she had. The client nodded with the expression of someone who will not be uncertain again for some time.

stories.headline: Gorge Files Wednesday Conditions; Fog in Excellent Standing; the Ridgeline Available for Those Who Ask Nicely
body: The Red River Gorge submitted its Wednesday report shortly before dawn, confirming fog in what observers are describing as 'a very composed autumn configuration.' The hollows have settled. The rock arches are present and not accepting appointments. The ridgeline, sources say, is in a receptive mood for those who approach with appropriate preparation and a working Jeep.
The enchanted Jeep itself spent Wednesday in the drive, resting. Steve noted that all systems are sound and that the Jeep 'seems content.' The Jeep declined to elaborate. No ducks have been moved.

stories.headline: Household Proceeds Through Wednesday Without Recorded Incident; Three Sources Independently Dispute This
body: The household submitted a clean Wednesday log by early evening — no incidents, no disruptions, biscuit tin at last count intact. However, three sources within the household, each interviewed separately, have indicated that something happened at approximately two in the afternoon involving the kitchen and at least one party who should not have been in the kitchen.

The sources disagree on the sequence of events. One source was asleep at the relevant time, which she considers evidence in her favor. One source believes the whole thing involved a reflection and not her at all. One source did not look up from the sofa. The biscuit tin has not been opened. The tin's exterior is warm. Investigation is ongoing.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Was not in the kitchen at two o'clock, has not been in the kitchen, cannot account for the warmth of the tin, and considers these questions a matter for the Ministry.
Ellie: There was another dog in the window again today — a very nice dog, very well-behaved — and Ellie would like it noted that she greeted her warmly and they had a lovely time.
Jersey: Wednesday presented two premium lap opportunities; Jersey accepted both without hesitation, sequentially, as a professional.
founding_editor_note: That hum you're hearing from the Ministry? A loose fitting on the resonance pipe. I'd have caught it in the first inspection. — D.

in_brief.sport: Wednesday's Wizarding Weightlifting Invitational reports a new standard has been set; the standard declines to name names but sources point toward Gringotts.
in_brief.forecast: Thursday: fog maintains its autumn residency; the hollows are keeping their own counsel; name tags expected to remain legible.

storyline_updates.title: The Briefcase
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: The briefcase has acquired a brass name tag on the clasp — not Quoyne's name, not any current Ministry employee. The tag begins with 'C' and is finely engraved. The Department of Mysteries said 'Ah' and withdrew. The briefcase has begun to hum faintly. Quoyne is filing this under Pending. No one has tried the lock. Day 4 (resolution): The briefcase should find its way — by its own apparent navigation — to Christine or to Gringotts. Its contents, when finally opened, should be a warm, funny payoff consistent with the Pulp Fiction glowing-briefcase easter egg tradition: something that makes complete sense in hindsight, is entirely Christine's, and which the Ministry will file under 'Wholesome, Misc.' once more.
